main_body: A tall, thin dark iron lamp-post pole (about 2px wide) with a horizontal crossbar at the top carrying two hanging yellow lanterns, and a small grey stone base at the bottom.
top_band: none: the pole is a 2px vertical dark line from row 4 to about 30, with no top surface or cap; the crossbar is a 1-2px dark line.
evidence: Reading down the centre column: a small ornament at rows 0-1, then a 1-2 row dark crossbar at rows 4-5, then a 2px dark pole down to the base. No horizontal surface is visible at the pole top or crossbar, only thin lines (rim only). The lanterns are drawn face-on with no visible top or lid. The base at rows 31-39 is a small grey block with a lighter top patch of about 2-3 rows, which is a small detail and not the main body. Overall a flat front elevation.

style.evidence: The pole is a flat dark 2px line with one tone and almost no shading. The lanterns have 3 yellow tones, but they are small and have a flat fill with dark near-black edges. The base is a few grey tones with little grain. Compared with the reference stall and well, which have rich tile scallops, wood grain and stone shading with many colours per tile, most tiles here are 2-4 colours of mostly empty background, so it is much thinner and flatter.
